title: 2028 Olympic Medal Predictions Based on Random Forest Model

source.pdf_page_offset_note: PDF page 1 is the summary sheet; PDF pages 2-25 are internally numbered solution pages 1-24; PDF pages 26-31 are the AI Use Report, internally numbered pages 25-30 and excluded from the official 25-page solution limit.

context_sources.use: Official medal-forecast, uncertainty, first-medal, event-program, host, coach, original-insight, data-use, page-limit, references, and AI-report requirements.
Five official data files used to audit schema, outcome grain, Samoa medal status, program-year metadata, and event-country medal deduplication.

limitations: PDF pages 1, 2, 8, 13, 16, 20, and 31 are image-layer or near-image-layer pages and were read from full-resolution renders.
Extracted text contains repeated QR-code and third-party watermark artifacts; central equations, tables, charts, and AI-report continuations were checked visually.
The paper supplies pseudocode but no runnable code, fitted model objects, hyperparameters, random seeds, complete prediction table, fold assignments, or reproducible result files.
The official data files themselves contain cross-file and metadata inconsistencies, including Samoa's retroactive 2008 medal and conflicting program terminal years.
All 31 paper pages and all four official problem pages were visually reviewed; critical feature, probability, count, host, coach, conclusion, and AI-use pages received full-resolution checks.
Third-party diagonal watermarks and QR blocks are treated as distribution artifacts rather than team-authored evidence.

forecast_deliverables: Predict at least gold and total medal counts for every country.
Measure model performance and provide uncertainty or precision estimates.
Forecast the full Los Angeles 2028 medal table with prediction intervals for all results.
Identify likely improvers and decliners relative to 2024.
first_medal_deliverables: Include countries that have never won an Olympic medal.
Predict how many will win their first medal in 2028 and provide odds.
program_deliverables: Relate event number and event type to country medal counts.
Identify important sports for various countries and explain why.
Estimate how host-chosen events affect results.
coach_deliverables: Find evidence of changes plausibly due to a great coach.
Estimate the coach contribution to medal counts.
Choose three country-sport investments and estimate each impact.
communication_deliverables: Provide original model-derived insights useful to National Olympic Committees.
Include a one-page summary, contents, complete solution, references, and an AI Use Report if AI is used.
task_reconstruction.paper_approach: Build lagged athlete capability features, train per-sport random forests for medal and gold labels, allocate event medals deterministically and by weighted Monte Carlo, reuse a modified random forest for first-medal countries, use Poisson-family regressions for event counts, use separate linear regressions for USA and China host effects, and define a before-after ordinal great-coach score.
task_reconstruction.coverage_gap: The paper gives intervals for only nine countries and point totals for ten; validates athlete classification rather than future country counts; misdefines and misclassifies the first-medal cohort; analyzes only two sport-country cases with duplicated athlete-row medals; does not identify the effect of host-selected event types; does not causally estimate coach effects or quantify all three recommendations; and omits the required references list.

section_map.summary: Reports top 2028 forecasts, first-medal probabilities, event and host claims, a great-coach claim, and broad validity language.
Lists assumptions, four task models, unique insights, and conclusions but no references section.
Continues Task 3, Task 4, insight, advantage, limitation, and conclusion entries.
Frames Olympic medal prediction and host advantage as an engaging multi-factor forecasting problem.
Restates medal, first-medal, event, host, coach, and NOC goals and shows the workflow.
Assumes historical stability, 2024-athlete continuity, no major shocks, negligible external effects, and accurate supplied data.
Defines athlete capability, event-level allocation, team-sport aggregation, gender coding, and NOC/Event one-hot features.
Defines four lagged historical features and introduces one-random-forest-per-sport modeling.
Copies 2024 participants and events to 2028, defines MedalBinary and GoldBinary targets, and uses random train/test splitting with fallbacks.
Applies encoded features, assigns deterministic podium positions, and introduces Monte Carlo sampling.
Draws event winners from fixed probabilities and reports top-nine 95-percent medal intervals.
Shows equestrian random-fold classification metrics and calls recall sensitivity.
Acknowledges high-probability overestimation, shows feature correlations, lists improvers/decliners, and begins first-medal classification.
Defines never-medaled status from athlete rows and reports random-forest accuracy/F1 charts by sport.
Simulates three winners per event, reports per-country probabilities, and estimates 4.78 new medal countries.

Uses athlete-row medal totals through 1964 and reports a coefficient of 0.0517.

Interprets beta times event count as elasticity and begins distribution-specification sensitivity.

contributions.summary: Decomposes a long official task into forecast, first-medal, event/host, coach, and NOC branches.
Uses shifted historical features to express prior athlete experience, best result, and weighted performance without intentionally using the current record.
Recognizes that athlete probabilities must pass through event-level medal constraints before country aggregation.
Produces outcome distributions rather than only one deterministic medal table.
Inspects ROC, PR, and calibration behavior and openly notes fold variability and high-probability overestimation.
Shows both the distribution of new-medal country counts and ranked per-country probabilities.
Compares Poisson, Negative Binomial, and zero-inflated specifications and reports leave-one-year-out influence.
Attempts to translate historical sport performance into country-specific coaching recommendations.
Discloses prompts and outputs used for assumption wording, model ideation, and strengths/limitations prose.

missing_edges: No cross-file reconciliation establishes the correct at-risk first-medal cohort or event-country medal grain.
No temporal backtest connects athlete classification performance to held-out country gold and total counts.
No uncertainty path covers roster turnover, event-program scenarios, calibration, parameters, preprocessing, or model specification in the reported intervals.
No country-sport alignment or counterfactual event program connects host choices to medal changes.
No control group, treatment timing design, or confounder adjustment connects coach arrival to medal-count effects.
No fitted effect, cost, or uncertainty connects the model to all three coaching investments.

assumptions.summary: Historical country and sport performance remains predictive through 2028.
assumptions.consequence: Regime changes and emerging programs are suppressed.
assumptions.verification: No rolling-origin country-count backtest is reported.

assumptions.summary: The 2024 athlete roster reappears in 2028 with stable ability.
assumptions.consequence: Retirements, injuries, qualification, and newcomers are omitted.
assumptions.verification: No roster scenario or attrition model is used.

assumptions.summary: No force majeure or material economic, political, or training-system shock occurs.
assumptions.consequence: Forecast intervals exclude major system shocks.

assumptions.summary: The five official data files are accurate and true.
assumptions.consequence: Cross-file contradictions and retroactive results are not reconciled.
assumptions.verification: Samoa and program-year metadata directly contradict the assumption.

assumptions.summary: Uncalibrated random-forest probabilities are adequate sampling weights despite observed overprediction at high probabilities.
assumptions.consequence: Medal and interval distributions inherit calibration bias.
assumptions.verification: Isotonic calibration is suggested but not applied.

assumptions.summary: Coach contribution is constant and the residual equals zero in the coach year.
assumptions.consequence: All deviation from a prior-three ordinal mean is assigned to the coach.
assumptions.verification: No control, timing, confounder, or placebo test is used.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Five supplied files are used without a documented key, schema, or cross-file reconciliation report.
Selected team sports are consolidated by country and year, but relays and repeated event-country medal rows remain embedded in athlete data.
Sex is mapped to a binary value and NOC and Event are one-hot encoded.
Cumulative medal counts, best score, and weighted ratio are shifted one record to approximate prior history.
The 2028 candidate roster and event distribution are copied from 2024.
Country medal history is derived from athlete rows instead of reconciled medal-count tables.
Samoa remains in the zero-medal cohort because its retroactive 2008 silver appears only in medal_counts, not the athlete row.
Relay-member medal rows are summed, giving 61 athlete medals and 45 gold rows in 18 events; event-medal deduplication gives 29 and 13.
Team-member rows give 11 medals in 2024; event-medal deduplication gives 6.
Podium categories are encoded 0-3 and averaged over three prior Games without a verified coach-tenure data table.
The official statement, dictionary, and delivered CSV disagree on whether event-program data extend beyond 2024.

models.summary: One binary medal and one binary gold random forest are trained per sport with NOC/Event identity and lagged athlete features.
Sports with fewer than five entries or one training class use historical average probabilities.
The highest gold probability receives gold and the next two medal probabilities receive silver and bronze.
Weighted draws without replacement allocate fixed podium slots from fitted probabilities.
A random forest models repeated static NOC ever-medaled labels and reuses its output as 2028 athlete medal probability.
USA swimming and China table-tennis athlete-row medal counts are modeled with a log link and event count predictor.
Negative Binomial and ZIP specifications are compared with Poisson by coefficient, log likelihood, and AIC.
Separate linear models regress country medals on host dummy, total events, and prior-three medal mean.
Coach effect is defined as current 0-3 podium score minus the prior-three-Games mean with zero residual.

verification.summary: Fixed-probability repeated draws estimate conditional outcome variation but not full predictive uncertainty.
Equestrian random-fold AUC and PR-AUC vary materially across folds, including PR-AUC 0.639 versus 0.926.
High fitted probabilities are observed to overpredict actual positives, but recalibration is not implemented before simulation.
Accuracy and F1 are reported by sport without a temporal or unseen-NOC split and do not validate first-medal transitions.
The 1964 USA swimming totals violate event-level medal bounds and expose athlete-row double counting.
The same USA swimming analysis reports coefficients 0.0517 and 0.1912 on adjacent pages.
The reported 21.1-percent increase matches exp(0.1912), not the printed exp(0.912).
Leave-one-year-out results expose 1964 influence but use only observations through 1964.
ZIP has the lowest AIC, but no held-out predictive comparison or count-grain correction is performed.
No panel control, pretrend, placebo, clustered error, or out-of-sample host-effect test is reported.
The stated USA effects 2 and 1.33 average to about 1.67, not 1.16.
A 2012 USA value is credited without applying the stated coach-tenure window.
An AI-generated false medal-distribution claim enters the final advantages section without correction.

results_trace.summary: USA, China, and Great Britain are forecast at 142/45, 113/42, and 69/15 total/gold medals.
Top-nine total and gold 95-percent intervals are shown, including USA total [113,142] and gold [37,53].
Ten point totals identify USA, China, and Italy as improvers and France, Australia, and Germany as decliners.
Samoa 0.406, Mali 0.266, and Guam 0.254 lead a first-medal list with expected count 4.78.
A 0.0517 coefficient is interpreted as about 5.3 percent more athlete-row medals per event.
A conflicting 0.1912 coefficient is interpreted as about 21.1 percent more per event.
Event count is nonsignificant with coefficient 0.1273 and p=0.59.
Hosting is attributed 74.7636 USA medals and 24.6836 China medals.
Lang Ping is assigned USA effects 2 and 1.33 with reported mean 1.16 and China effect 1.67.
India badminton/hockey, Sweden swimming, and Romania rowing are recommended, but only India receives a rough medal range.

writing_logic.summary: The summary maps its four task labels to methods and headline outputs, supporting rapid scanning.
The workflow provides a useful high-level task decomposition.
Named, plain-language feature definitions make the forecast pipeline easier to reconstruct.
ROC, PR, and calibration are discussed together, including a real calibration concern rather than only strengths.
LOO and alternative count distributions are colocated with the main event-count claim.
Coach investment recommendations are presented before their effects, costs, and uncertainty are actually estimated.
Advantages repeat AI-polished claims that conflict with the fixed roster, per-sport method, and untested overfitting.
The required references list is absent, breaking claim and visual provenance.

language_observations.summary: Concrete numbers improve usefulness, but scientific, reasonable, feasible, and validity exceed the available tests.
The claim that the structure ensures accurate predictions precedes any prospective validation.
Excellent and proves overstate random-fold discrimination and obscure a weak PR fold and calibration error.
Contributes to converts a confounded positive coefficient into a causal event-program claim.
Increases by reports sparse observational coefficients as causal medal effects.
Demonstrates validity uses the same example that defines the effect and has arithmetic and timing errors.
Underdeveloped regions is neither operationalized from supplied data nor connected to a tested decision model.
Fluent AI-refined strengths are reproduced without method-to-claim verification.

visualization_observations.summary: A compact workflow makes the official task decomposition visible.
Athlete photos and radar charts consume space and use mixed axes without explaining predictive relevance or uncertainty.
A sorted country bar chart communicates relative predicted medal counts but lacks intervals on the same view.
Gold and total interval bars show uncertainty for leading countries but not all requested results.
ROC, PR, and calibration curves expose discrimination and probability bias, but fold sample sizes and interval bands are absent.
Three correlation heatmaps are aligned and labeled, though they do not establish causal importance.
Accuracy and F1 bars summarize many sport models but obscure temporal leakage and target mismatch.
The histogram plus sorted probability bars is an appropriate pair for count and unit-level rare-event results.
A word cloud redundantly and imprecisely encodes the same probabilities and omits uncertainty.
LOO coefficients and side-by-side distribution metrics provide useful model-audit views despite invalid input grain.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: A task-numbered summary with concrete forecasts may have improved scanability, but no judge evidence attributes the award to it.
Including ROC, PR, calibration, LOO, and alternative distributions may signal verification effort, although the tests do not match the final targets.
Prompt-level AI disclosure satisfies a visible compliance expectation, but the award does not validate the copied AI claims.

weaknesses.summary: The fixed 2024 roster and stable-world assumptions are not included in prediction uncertainty.
Cross-file anomalies are assumed away despite an explicit official warning.
Random row splits leak repeated entities and eras into prospective evaluation.
Event-specific award rules, teams, relays, ties, quotas, and double-bronze sports are not documented.
Intervals represent fixed-probability outcome draws rather than full predictive uncertainty and are not provided for all countries.
Known high-probability overestimation is not corrected before simulation.
Ever-medaled NOC status is repeated across athlete rows and mislabeled as a future first-medal event.
Already-medaled Samoa is the top alleged first-medal candidate, invalidating the expected count.
The word cloud is redundant and quantitatively weak.
Relay/team members are double counted, producing impossible event-level medal totals.
Coefficient and exponent reporting are internally inconsistent.
A level-dependent elasticity is misread as an increasing one-event effect.
Mechanical opportunity and time confounding are interpreted causally despite only data through 1964.
Team-member rows again inflate the country medal outcome.
Sparse per-country regressions cannot identify host causality or host-selected event effects.
Ordinal podium scores are treated as cardinal medal contribution and all residual change is assigned to the coach.
The USA average is arithmetically wrong and includes a post-tenure year.
Three recommended investments lack fitted impacts, intervals, costs, and decision criteria.
Regional-development and event-addition claims are unsupported by supplied variables or feasibility analysis.
The required references list is missing.
An AI-generated false medal-allocation rule and overstated strengths enter the final paper without independent verification.

independent_extensions.summary: Build an entity-key contract and convert athlete rows to event-NOC-medal awards before any country-count model; assert award-count invariants per event.
Use rolling Olympic cutoffs, athlete/NOC grouping, and full bottom-up aggregation to backtest country gold and total forecasts on several held-out Games.
Calibrate out-of-fold probabilities, simulate event-specific award rules, and combine parameter, roster, program, and model uncertainty with outcome randomness.
Model first-medal acquisition as a discrete-time NOC-Games hazard over a reconciled at-risk set, then validate calibration and expected counts by rolling origin.
Model medal rate or share with event opportunities as exposure, time/country structure, correct count grain, and out-of-sample comparisons rather than raw athlete-row totals.
Estimate host and coach effects with panel/event-study or synthetic-control designs, verified treatment dates, comparison groups, pretrends, placebos, and uncertainty.
Maintain a machine-checkable deliverable matrix that fails when all-country intervals, quantified three-country impacts, references, or other official clauses are absent.
Map every AI interaction to adopted text, model, equation, or code and independently verify domain facts, data constraints, mathematics, claims, and tests before submission.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: A second C paper shows that untested stability, roster, data, and residual assumptions must trigger scenarios and non-use conditions.
Expands estimand discipline from ecological risk to athlete, country-count, first-event, ordinal, and causal targets.
Adds coefficient, exponent, average, event-count, and interval invariants.
Separates outcome simulation from roster, program, parameter, calibration, and structural uncertainty.
Requires temporal target-level validation rather than random intermediate classification metrics.
Adds point/interval, expected-count, and causal-effect semantic checks.
Extends recommendation lineage to coach investment and NOC program advice.
Adds probabilistic forecasts, diagnostic curves, and prohibition of redundant word clouds.
Adds forecasting, classification, count, causal, and AI-polished overclaim diagnostics.
Adds statistical-grain, key, cross-file reconciliation, and hard counting invariants.
Adds cutoff-safe temporal features, grouped splits, rolling backtests, and roster/program scenarios.
Adds a correct at-risk cohort and discrete-time first-occurrence model.
Adds calibrated constrained simulation and decomposed predictive uncertainty.
Adds exposure-aware count modeling and guards against mechanical opportunity effects.
Adds intervention timing, comparison groups, panel designs, placebos, and causal claim gates.
Adds official requirement, data restriction, references, and all-results coverage gates.
Adds prompt-to-artifact mapping and independent verification of AI-assisted work.

unresolved_questions: What exact preprocessing code produced team, relay, and event-level samples for the random forests?
Were shifted features grouped by athlete and Olympic year so multiple same-year rows could not leak current-Games results?
What hyperparameters, seeds, fold assignments, sample counts, and calibration procedure produced the reported metrics and intervals?
Why is the USA point total exactly the upper endpoint of its reported 95-percent interval?
How many countries received complete gold and total intervals outside the nine displayed?
Why were USA swimming observations after 1964 excluded from the Poisson analysis?
Which of 0.0517 and 0.1912 is the intended USA swimming coefficient?
How were coach tenure dates verified, and why was USA 2012 attributed to Lang Ping?
What model generated the India, Sweden, and Romania coach-impact claims?
How were official data contradictions and the missing post-2024 program columns handled in code?
